patch.x-ms-description-for-model: Use this tool to update an existing Microsoft Planner task. You must send a request body containing at least one field to change, such as title, dueDateTime, startDateTime, percentComplete, or bucketId. An empty body is rejected. Include only the fields you intend to change; any field you omit is left unchanged. Example intents: 'Mark the Review Q4 budget task 50% complete', 'Move my Planner task to the Done bucket'

priority.description: Priority of the task. Valid range of values is between 0 and 10 (inclusive), with increasing value being lower priority (0 has the highest priority and 10 has the lowest priority). Currently, Planner interprets values 0 and 1 as "urgent", 2 and 3 and 4 as "important", 5, 6, and 7 as "medium", and 8, 9, and 10 as "low". Currently, Planner sets the value 1 for "urgent", 3 for "important", 5 for "medium", and 9 for "low".

title.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to a short, clear task title (up to 255 characters). Examples: Review Q4 budget, Prepare slides for weekly status

bucketId.description: The bucket to place this task in.
bucketId.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to the bucket ID of the bucket where the task should appear. If unspecified or unsure, leave empty for default placement.

startDateTime.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to the start date/time of the task in ISO 8601 format. Leave empty if not specified. Example: 2025-11-28T09:00:00Z

dueDateTime.description: The datetime the task is due (Ex. '2018-04-13T00:42:19.284Z').
dueDateTime.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to the due date/time in ISO 8601 format. Leave empty if not specified. Example: 2025-12-31T17:00:00Z

assignments.description: Semi-colon separated ids or email addresses of users to assign this task to.
assignments.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to assignees as semicolon-separated emails or user IDs. Leave empty if none specified. Example: alice@contoso.com;bob@contoso.com

priority.description: Priority of the task. Valid range of values is between 0 and 10 (inclusive), with increasing value being lower priority (0 has the highest priority and 10 has the lowest priority). Currently, Planner interprets values 0 and 1 as "urgent", 2 and 3 and 4 as "important", 5, 6, and 7 as "medium", and 8, 9, and 10 as "low". Currently, Planner sets the value 1 for "urgent", 3 for "important", 5 for "medium", and 9 for "low".
priority.x-ms-description-for-model: Set this to priority of the task from 0 (highest priority) to 10 (lowest priority). Typical values to use: 1=Urgent, 3=Important, 5=Medium, 9=Low. If you cannot infer priority from request, set to 5.
